summary: Ovda Airport serves the resort city of Eilat in southern Israel, situated in the arid Negev desert roughly 60 km north of the city center. Originally built as a military airbase, it was opened to limited civilian traffic to relieve pressure on Eilat's smaller municipal airfield. The airport primarily handles seasonal charter and low-cost European flights, though many civilian operations have shifted to the newer Ramon International Airport.
faqs:
Q: How far is Ovda Airport from Eilat city center?
A: Ovda Airport is approximately 60 km (37 miles) north of Eilat, requiring about a 1-hour drive through desert terrain.

Q: What airlines operate from Ovda Airport?
A: Mainly seasonal charter carriers and some European low-cost airlines have historically served Ovda, though many have transitioned to Ramon International Airport.

Q: Is Ovda Airport still open to civilian flights?
A: Civilian traffic at Ovda has been significantly reduced since Ramon International Airport opened in 2019, but it remains operational as a military facility and handles some charter services.

Q: Are there facilities like lounges or restaurants in the terminal?
A: The terminal is small and basic, offering limited amenities such as a cafeteria and duty-free shop suited to its seasonal charter operations.
transport_tips: The most practical option to reach Eilat from Ovda is by pre-booked shuttle bus or taxi, as public transport connections are limited. Rental cars are available but the long desert drive requires careful planning, especially at night. Many tour operators include airport transfers when booking Eilat holiday packages.
local_tip: If flying into Ovda on a charter, keep your camera ready on the descent—the final approach passes over dramatic desert ridges and the Eilat mountain range, offering some of the best aerial views of the Negev landscape.
